utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, have Colonel Blaskic brought in, please. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good morning to the interpreters. I assume everybody can hear me. Good morning to the Prosecution and to the Defence and to the accused. I would like to say that this is going to be a somewhat long morning, we'll take a 10-minute break at 11.00 and then a 20-minute break; is that all right with the interpreters? Wonderful, everybody is happy with that. We can then immediately move to giving the floor to Mr. Nobilo who will take his place at the bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Our next witness, the witness of the Defence, is Brigadier Ivica Zeko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You said Ivica?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Zeko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the course of these proceedings for more than one year we have received very little or no information about the development, strength and deployment of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the area of relevance for the indictment and in the time that is referred to in the indictment. For that purpose, and in order to define the development, command structure, areas of responsibility and the way in which those zones moved, or rather the movement of the BH units, as they progressed, advanced or withdrew, we asked Brigadier Ivica Zeko, who was in 1992, 1993 assistant commander of the operative zone of central Bosnia for intelligence. Therefore, he was the assistant of the accused for intelligence and a member of the staff of the operative zone of central Bosnia. Brigadier Zeko is today a brigadier in the Army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is the joint army which developed from the BH army and the HVO. So, he is in the Croatian component of the Federation Army. I hope that this will be sufficient by way of an introduction, and could we please have the witness brought in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, Registrar, have Brigadier Ivica Zeko brought in, please. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please remain standing for a few moments. First tell us your name, your given name, current profession and place of residence, if possible, and then you will read your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, my name is Ivica Zeko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are a bit far from the microphone. Would you please approach the microphone and speak a little louder so the interpreters can hear you. Please remain standing, however, but get closer to the microphone. I know it's a little complicated. Speak louder, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm Ivica Zeko. I was born on the 12th of June, 1961 in the village of Sebisic, the Municipality of Novi Travnik. I am now serving in the Army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please remain standing for a few moments to read the solemn declaration that the usher is handing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You may be seated. Thank you for having come to the Tribunal. Please be seated. You have come at the request of the Defence counsel for the accused who is present in this courtroom, General Blaskic. You are going to answer, the major questions will be asked by Mr. Nobilo, and then you will answer the questions asked by the Office of the Prosecutor and the questions of the Judges. Mr. Nobilo, the floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Nobilo:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, good morning, and on behalf of the Defence I thank you for accepting the call. You told the Court where you were born and where you are living, but could you tell us about yourself, your educational background and what you were doing before the war in the area of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I graduated from the secondary military school in Sarajevo. I then went on to the military academy of the ground forces in Belgrade, after which my first position was in the Republic of Slovenia, in the Postajna Garrison where I held the duty of commander of a reconnaissance company until the beginning of the war in Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your rank in the JNA before you abandoned it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I had the rank of captain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you leave, and when?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: As the fighting started and as the JNA took up a position against the people in the month of July 1991 I left Slovenia and went to Germany.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, you left the JNA because you saw that that was not the place for you, you went to Germany and you could have stayed in Germany. Why did you decide to go back to the former Yugoslavia, or more particularly to Bosnia, and when?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, having been called by the defence department of Novi Travnik in the month of February 1992 I reported to the office where I was assigned to join up with the work of the Territorial Defence in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, I know I did tell to you speak slowly, but you can speed up a little bit. We must not overdo it. What happened next? When did you start working in the headquarters of the operative zone for central Bosnia, and what were your particular tasks there?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, until the month of March 1991 my duties were linked to the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You probably made a mistake, you weren't referring to '91.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that was just the point I wanted to make, you must have made a slip.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was in 1992. I then moved to the municipal headquarters of the HVO in Novi Travnik, and I stayed there until July 1992. After.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: When the operative zone for central Bosnia was formed I transferred to Vitez to the command of the operative zone of central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the operative zone, the command of the operative zone, was it then in Vitez or in Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the command was in Kruscica, but as this is all part of the Vitez municipality, that is why I said Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What position were you assigned to in the operative zone?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: At the time assistant Chief of Staff of the Headquarters for Intelligence Affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe that position very briefly, as we're not military experts? What did you actually do within your duties in the operative zone of central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In the operative zone of central Bosnia my duties were to organise the department for intelligence, which would later on collect information about the enemy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your department was after a short time moved from Kruscica to Hotel Vitez, and from there to another place where you set up your offices for intelligence?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. When the command was moved to the hotel in Vitez my department was set up, and following the orders of the commander it was established in the place called Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is where it remained until the end of the war; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, will you tell the Court by way of introduction what methods did you use to collect data, which you will shortly begin to present to us? I'm talking about the period of '92, '93; what methods did you apply to obtain the information you needed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, in my work I used methods such as teamwork, reconnaissance, observation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment please, let us clarify these terms. What is the difference between reconnaissance and observation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The difference is that reconnaissance is done by entering into enemy territory, and observation is done from the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue. What other methods were used to gain information about the enemy?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I have mentioned observation, then electronic devices were used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us exactly what that means?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It means collecting data about the enemy using enemy lines, intercepting enemy lines, or simply tapping enemy communications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other methods of collecting data?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, we used the media, radio, television, printed media, minutes from meetings held with representatives of international organisations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use refugees, displaced persons, citizens who may come from enemy territory to your own territory as a source of information?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I will put to you a rather delicate question now, but tell me in very general terms, because I believe neither the Court nor the Prosecution will ask you for names; did you have a network of agents in the enemy territory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, let us now go on to the substance of your testimony. Will you please, using the ELMO and the monitors and the screen, and using the laser pointer, if necessary, you may freely get up and move over to the model in relief, present to us your memories, or as best you remember, the development of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in '92, '93 in the municipalities of Travnik, Novi Travnik, Vitez, Busovaca and Kiseljak. May the lights be dimmed so we can have better visibility of the screen? Just a moment, please. Can you see the picture on your monitor?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, Your Honours, on this slide we have a map of Bosnia-Herzegovina with the areas in pink being the territories under the control of the army of the Bosnian Serbs. The green areas are the territories under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And in yellow the territory under the control of the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council. In this red rectangle is the area consisting of two enclaves, the Lasva and the Lepenica valleys, which we shall be discussing. And this is the area also depicted on the model.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You need to press twice.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This map in mauve, again we have the territories under the control of the Bosnian Serbs. Green is the territory under the control of the BH army, and yellow within this small red square, the area in yellow is the territory of the Lasva River valley, Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which municipalities are those?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Travnik, Vitez and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, what does this map depict? What is the period of time and which are the symbols used?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This map, Your Honours, covers the period from the 24th of April to the 24th of May 1992, and the map marks in red the units of the army of the Republika Srpska. The green are the units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the units of the Croatian Defence Council are depicted in blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those days did the name of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina exist, or were some other terms still used, like the Territorial Defence, and so on?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In this period the name used was Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. You say that the square represents what portion of the territory? I'm not able to read it here?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this rectangle shows the territory consisting of Novi Travnik, Travnik, Vitez and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, for your own orientation, on the left-hand side where the Serbs are, marked in red is Travnik, closer is Travnik, in the middle is Vitez and Busovaca and so on. Can I show you on the model?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's not necessary, because I didn't understand what the square meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This rectangle is the same as the first rectangle on the relief.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The first step towards the formation of the future army of Bosnia-Herzegovina can be considered to have been taken at he beginning of 1991. Actually, the Territorial Defence was still functioning on the basis of laws and regulations taken over from the former Yugoslavia, which was still in force. The police forces or the force of the MUP, the Ministry of the Interior; units of the patriotic league; units of the Green Berets; and the forces of MOS, Muslim Armed Forces. On the 9th of April, 1992, the presidency at the time decided to jointly conduct and command and form the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, consisted of district staffs. The district TO staff Zenica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I think you can speak a bit more quickly. We can follow you. When it's very slow it's difficult to follow.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The District Staff of the Zenica Territorial Defence consisting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I see, what was just said about Judge Riad on the transcript, I agree with it, since it was Judge Riad said it I will say it again so it is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: This is, of course, not to say we're going to go against the instructions of the Presiding Judge that you ask not to go too slow. It's like the artillery, you can go too far, too slowly, you have to find the middle ground. There you go, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Riad. INTERPRETER: The interpreter suggests that the witness take his head phones off.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the District Staff of TO Zenica consists of the following municipalities: Gorni Vakuf, Bugojno, Donj Vakuf, Travnik, Novi Travnik, Vitez, Busovaca, Kakanj and Zenica. The Municipal Staff of the TO of Travnik consisted of detachments. The territorial detachment of Gradina with the command post in the village of Bijelo Bucje. The territorial detachment of Turbe with its command post in Turbe; the territorial detachment Karaule with its command post in Karaule; the first and second Travnik detachment with its command posts in Travnik; the territorial detachment Han Bila with the command post in Han Bila; the territorial detachment Ljuta Greda with the command post in the village of Kapelici; the territorial detachment Mehurici with its command post in the village of Mehurici. All these detachments were varied in strength between 400 and 500 members, with the exception of the first and second Travnik detachments which numbered about 1.500 members.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, our client is taking an active part in the proceedings and he is telling me that almost all the places mentioned by the witness have been left out. And the positions of the territorial defence detachments in space are very important for a subsequent understanding of events. What should we do now? Should we proceed and then deal with the transcript later on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yesterday we had transcript problems. I would like to thank the accused; of course, it's his right to point this out. What's going on here, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: When we're talking about proper names, there is immediately going to be a correction once the hearing is over and then the transcript is made available to both the parties and to you and ordinarily the transcript will have all of the towns and cities that were noted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I think in general the transcribers who have to work very, very quickly, when they're not sure of a name, I think that's what it is, is when they're not sure of a name.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think they may just even type in any letter or leave a blank. But they know that right away they've got to correct it. I want to take advantage in order to thank those individuals who are transcribing our work. We often see them leaving the Tribunal two or three hours after the hearings are complete because everything is looked at again. The accused can be assured that the names will be properly put in, and, in addition, the Defence will receive copies of the final transcript should any other corrections be necessary. You may go on now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue, Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Your Honours, in addition to these detachments, under the command of the Municipal Staff in Travnik, there were also the following units: The units of the Patriotic League of the Green Berets, of the Muslim armed forces, members of the MUP or the Ministry of the Interior. Towards the end of May, 1992, in the Territory of Travnik, two brigades arrived from the Republic of Croatia. The 1st Krajina Brigade formed in Zagreb, armed and equipped with its commander Osman Osmanovic and the 7th Krajina Brigade formed in Rijeka, under the command of Fikret Cuskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, these brigades that you mentioned were formed, equipped and organised in the Republic of Croatia in the towns of Rijeka and Zagreb and that they came to the Territory of Travnik. Who were the members of those brigades, in ethnic terms?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In ethnic terms, the members were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The staff of this command was in Travnik, in the barracks there.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The municipal command of Territorial Defence of Novi Travnik was formed with three detachments. The first detachment with the command post in Travnik; the second detachment had its command post in the Village of Petcui (Phoen). And the third command post had its command post in the village of Opara. In addition to these detachments -- the third detachment, I'm sorry -- in addition to these detachments, let me just state that these detachments had been 450 to 500 men. In addition to these detachments, under the command of the Municipal Staff of Novi Travnik there were other units of the Patriotic League, the Green Berets, the Muslim Armed Forces and members of MUP, the Internal Affairs Ministry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, let us take a pause here. First of all, I am interested in your assessments. Do you have any records that you made in Travnik? At the time in Travnik, how many Territorial Defence forces were there on the other units which you mentioned under the command of the staff of the Territorial Defence of the town, how many soldiers at that time were there? If you can give an assessment.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Well, I said a moment ago, I told you of the strength of each detachment, how many men each detachment had. And the other units that existed in the locality, the 1st and the 7th Klein of brigades, which, later on, were to join forces to become the 70th Brigade and they had 3.300 soldiers at that time. I did not add up all the forces, so I don't have the end figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The second question, which I would like to ask you is the following: You mentioned the Krajina Brigades, which we'll see played an important role later on; particularly, the 1st and the 7th. You said they were formed in Zagreb. In Zagreb and Preocica, were they formed on the basis of a private initiative or did the Croatian government authorise this and equip these units?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I don't know how they were established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And one more piece of information, which I think is important to state at the beginning as far as the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina is concerned, before the conflict with the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in April of 1993, did you come by this data through your intelligence work or in some other way, would you explain this to the Court please; so the data on the armies of Bosnia-Herzegovina, before the conflict, did they have a status of an enemy and did you do any intelligence work towards them?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, before the conflict I said in my presentation that I worked in the Territorial Defence department, and, after that, we worked together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is we? When you say "we" who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The HVO and the Territorial Defence of the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you want to say, and please put me right if I am wrong, is that as you were allies and had joint operations and cooperated, you knew their data and information and they knew yours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I interrupted you, you were in Novi Travnik, so you can continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In addition to the detachment, I said there were units of the Patriotic League, the Green Berets and the Muslim Armed Forces and units of MUP, the Internal Affairs Ministry. The Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence of Vitez was composed of two detachments of Territorial Defence and one manoeuvre battalion. The first detachment incorporated the villages of Kruscica, Prasca, Gacice, with the command post in Kruscica. The second detachment encompassed Poculice, Vranjska, Bukve, Sivrino Silo, Ahmici and Pirici. The command post of this detachment was located in Poculice. The manoeuvre battalion with the command post in Vitez, that was where that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Brigadier, how strong the forces in Vitez were? What about the second detachment and the manoeuvre battalion?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The first detachment had 650 men, that is to say about 650; the second had approximately 700 and the manoeuvre battalion had 300 members and the commander was Ahmed Kulenovic a former officer of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the "manoeuvre detachment," what does that mean? What is the difference between the territorial units and the manoeuvre detachment or mobile detachment?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This unit was mobile and could be effective on the whole region, not only territorially, so it can be used elsewhere as well. It was a mobile detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "mobile," it means that they were not to defend a given territory, but to be mobile and to go to other localities where needed. You mentioned the villages, does that mean that the units were located in the villages, in each of the villages you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The Municipal Staff of the TO of Busovaca, was formed with two detachments: The first detachment had its command post in the Village of Busovaca; the second detachment had its command post in the Village of Kacuni. And there was one independent unit, which was the size of a company and it incorporated the villages of Buselji, Donja Rovna and Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, you said that the first detachment had its command post in the city of Bosnia, not in Merdani? That was a slip?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, Merdani, I'm sorry, the command post was in the village of Merdani and the second detachment had its command post in the Village of Kacuni. The Municipal Staff of the TO was in Busovaca. In addition to these attachments, under the Territorial Defence staff of Busovaca there were other units as well of the Patriotic League and the Muslim armed forces, as well as the units of MUP, the Internal Affairs Ministry. In this municipality there were no units of the Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mention the different units, is it true that all the units were under the command of the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: As a conclusion from what I have presented, we can note that the zone of responsibility of the Municipal Staff of the TO of Zenica and the zone of responsibility, the district of responsibility, were superimposed on this territory -- overlapped on this territory. On this slide -- Mr. President, once again in the transcript the sense, the witness said that the two territories, the zone of responsibility of the District Staff of Territorial Defence of Zenica overlapped with the zone of responsibility of the operative zone of the HVO for Central Bosnia, they overlapped, and can we ask the witness whether that is exact.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the same territory was the zone of responsibility of two armies, that's what you wanted to say. Thank you, please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, on this map, you can see the distribution and activities of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina from the 15th of October to the 25th of October, 1992. The distribution of the units remains the same, but they are strengthened in this period of time because there was a daily influx of refugees from the Bosanska-Krajina region, that is to say under the control of the Republic of Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These refugees, what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They were of the Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The second thing that characterises the particular was that the first foreigners arrived and they became included into the Muslim armed forces, particularly in the area of the Municipality of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you specify some of the localities which became the basis of these foreign citizens?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The start was in Travnik, first of all Travnik, the Medresa facility and in the old town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me, where do these foreigners come from? Were they also Muslims? Were they foreigners? Were they refugees from other countries? On the Serb side, for example.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: For the most part they were from the Arab countries, Iran and Afghanistan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us clarify this matter. Please tell us how you call them or they call themselves, these fighters who came from the Arab states from Iran and Afghanistan?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: We're going to say something about that later on, but for the most part they called themselves the Mujehadeen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have some separate characteristics as to uniform, beards and so on? Is it the same thing that we see in (inaudible) in Afghanistan?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: That is what they looked like visually, they had beards; they had the caps on their heads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue, yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This period was also characterised by the territory between the local Muslims and the Muslims who had arrived from the areas of the Krajina, Bosanska-Krajina region. And the situation became complicated in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, you can use your notes quite freely, and place them in front of you. That is standard procedure in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: At this time, we had -- two incidents broke out. The first incident occurred on the 18th of October, 1992, in Novi Travnik. The first armed conflict to take over the Petrol pump.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between whom did the armed -- the incident break out?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The incident was between the units of the Territorial Defence and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The second incident occurred on the 20th of October on the road between Busovaca and Vitez. The TO Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina placed a watch-point and failed to allow the HVO people to move towards Jajce. Two days afterwards, this checkpoint was disbanded and the shift for Jajce could pass through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, there were different interpretations in the course of these proceedings as to whether the HVO army, which was stopped in Ahmici in October 1992, whether they were to go towards Jajce in the front towards the Serbs or whether it was to go to the assistance of the HVO groups in Novi Travnik. That is a debatable point. You say that it was on its way to Jajce, how do you know that it was on its way to Jajce?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Well, I know this because I saw that it passed and left for Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after the conflict it, in fact, went to Jajce?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: On this slide, you can see the period from the second of November 1992 to the 5th of January, 1993. In this time period, the forces of the Army of Republic of Srpska in the 1st Krajina Corps, to be more exact, at the end of October, began their offensive on Jajce. So that in this period of time, there was a great wave of refugees from Bosanska-Krajina. And I show here the areas from which the refugees came for the most part, Kotor Varos, Sanski Most, Banja Luka, Prijedor, Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, I apologise for interrupting you again, but let us go back a moment. When you speak about refugees, I know it is not essential, but as we are dealing with an international armed conflict and a civil war, for the purposes of the proceedings, may we know the ethnicities of the majority of these 200.000 refugees?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: For the most part these refugees were of the Muslim nationality, Muslim ethnicity, although with the downfall of Jajce, there were some Croats as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what is the difference between refugees, Muslims and Croat refugees? Where do one go and what direction did the others go?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Well, after the downfall of Jajce itself, we'll be able to see this more clearly. On the 2nd of November, 1992, when the refugees of Muslim ethnicity, mostly, a portion stayed in Travnik, Novi Travnik and Vitez area and another portion went to Busovaca and the surrounding villages of Zenica, around Zenica, Bila. The Croat refugees and the army together with them, went towards Herzegovina, in the direction of Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, this wave of refugees, we saw that the Croatian refugees with the soldiers did not remain in the locality, but went towards the south, to Herzegovina, so this wave of Muslim refugees, and I suppose the able-bodied men and soldiers, did they make up larger units of Territorial Defence and can you tell us what the situation numerically was like according to the different municipalities? The numeric status of the units in Travnik, Novi Travnik and that area, Vitez, Busovaca and so on.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This period was characterised by more and more refugees coming in, which meant that the number of military able-bodied men increased. And that was what guided the presidency of the day in Bosnia-Herzegovina to make a decision on the formation of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And to have it made up of five corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we start talking about the corps, could we, if you have the facts and figures -- I know it's difficult to remember everything -- at the end of the day how the individual brigades, how many soldiers did they have? Could you give us an overall view of the numerical state of the units?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The brigades were still not formed. They were still territorial detachments. But the number of every territorial detachment, as well as units, the units that existed under the municipal staff increased in number from one day to the next. So it was impossible to know the exact number and have statistics on this. One detachment, which might have had 5 to 600 men now have 800 or 900 men if you look at one unit. But if you take them all together, I haven't got the exact total amount.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we can say there was a significant increase in the number of soldiers and sometimes the numbers were even doubled. Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In this period, as I said earlier on, the presidency of the day on the 3rd of September, 1992, took the decision to set up an Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was composed of five corps. The 3rd Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was set up on the 1st of December, 1992, in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This corps, did it cover the same zone of responsibility as the District Staff of Zenica, like the Operative Zone of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The 3rd Corps with a command post in Zenica had its organisational structure as follows, the command of the corps, the staff, with the other units of the military police, the links, communications division, the engineering battalion, the company, ABHO. The brigades were composed of the following mountain brigades, a mechanised brigade. A detachment, special MUP units, which were called the manoeuvre units, and auxiliary units such as the logistics brigade, the artillery division the anti-aircraft division, the armoured division. Under the command of the Corps and within the composition of the 3rd Corps was the 7th Muslim Motorised Brigade the El Mudzhid Unit and here I have not indicated the Abdul Atif Unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, would you please explain to the Court what the characteristics are of the 7th Muslim Motorised Brigade, the El Mudzahid Unit and the Abdul Atif Unit?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the characteristics of the 7th Muslim Brigade was that it was made up of the members of purely those individuals which adhered to all the religious rights and customs in the unit. Therefore, these were exclusively those members, no other members but the Muslims made up that particular brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But not Muslims, if I have understood you correctly, as a nationality as an ethnicity, but Orthodox Muslims, Orthodox believers?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the foreign citizens that you mentioned, where were they in this composition?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They were in the El Mudzahid Unit and the other one I mentioned the Abdul Atif Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, we're going to take a short break for about ten minutes to allow the interpreters to continue this long morning. All right, let's take our break for the ten minutes and suspend the hearing now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed, please have the accused brought in. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, before we continue with your presentation we can see here the organisational set up of the 3rd Corps; could you explain to the Court what is the difference or what is the advantage, whichever you like, regarding the organisational set up? What was the difference between the Territorial Defence and the HVO? How can you explain that in a relatively short period of time the BH army managed to build up its entire military structure?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Your Honours, the organisation of the Territorial Defence and of the BH army was inherited from the former system so that it was much easier to set it up. Actually, all that was done was to fill in the units with men, according to the previous organisational structure, and to set up additional ones in view of the larger number of men that were joining up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereas the HVO, it had to start from scratch; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, will you please continue this discussion about the 3rd Corps. We were talking about its structure, the composition of the Muslim units, El Mudzahid and the Abdul Atif Unit.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I couldn't hear the interpretation, I was listening to the French. So, could you repeat, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was saying that the HVO did not have the advantage of the Territorial Defence because it had to build up its structure from scratch; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I went on to say, could you continue your presentation and discussion of the 3rd Corps as you had planned?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Your Honours, let me briefly go back a little bit to the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Brigadier, you can speed up a little bit. I know that this happened far in the past. Mr. Nobilo has told us what you're going to talk about, time is essential for all of us; so, could you please speed up a little bit? Be clear, be a little more dynamic. So will you make a little effort, please?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's my mistake, the witness speaks naturally very fast, so I kept cautioning him not to speak so fast in the courtroom and he is taking me a little too seriously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's not, I must say, it's not a question of speed. It's true there are witnesses who speak quickly and others slowly, but it's a question of expressing his thoughts. Could you be a little more concrete in your ideas and respond to Mr. Nobilo's questions? Because sometimes it's not very clear. So, Mr. Nobilo, will you pinpoint your question so that we can proceed in a more efficient manner?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next slide shows the units and their command posts. The command post in Zenica, the headquarters and support units in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: There are no particular comments regarding this slide, Mr. Nobilo, except if someone has a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, but I wanted the witness to describe the structure of 3rd Corps and to situate the units in space, because this will be of importance later on for an understanding of the events, all these units, the brigades, of course, which are the greatest interest, the 7th Muslim and the El Mudzahid. We can neglect the units attached to headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where they were located in terms of territory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The commands of the brigades were as follows: The 303rd Brigade, command place in Zenica; the 323rd Light Brigade in Kiseljak; the 306th Light Brigade with a command post in Han Bila. The mountain brigades: The 302nd had its command post in Zenica; the 303rd, also in Zenica; the 304th also in Zenica -- I'm sorry, 314th. The 304th Brigade had its command post in Breza; the 309th Mountain Brigade had its command post in Kakanj; the 310th Mountain Brigade had its command post in Fojnica; the 319th Mountain Brigade with the command post in Zepce; the 312th Mountain Brigade with command post in Travnik; the 308th Mountain Brigade with its command post in Novi Travnik; 325th Mountain Brigade with its command post in Vitez; the 328th Mountain Brigade with its command post in Zavidovici; the 333rd Mountain Brigade with its command post in Busovaca; the 350th Mountain Brigade with its command post in Zenica. This is also a Jajce brigade, as it was composed of displaced persons from Jajce by the Municipal Staff of Jajce. The 317th Mountain Brigade with its command post in Gornj Vakuf; the 307th Mountain Brigade with its command post in Bugojno; the 17th Krajina Mountain Brigade with its command post in Travnik; and the 27th Krajina brigade with its command post in Travnik, also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These mountain brigades were founded as early as December 1992; weren't they?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the strength of the individual brigades and their zones of responsibility, rather which areas those brigades covered?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. But, Mr. President, I will go back to the previous slide. The 312th Brigade consisting of the first and second Travnik detachment with a command post in Travnik had a zone of responsibility here facing the army of the Bosnian Serbs. And in depth, the strength of this brigade was between 3.200 and 3.500 men. The 306th Brigade, which was composed of the detachments from the TO of Ljuta Greda, Mehurici, Han Bila, with a command post in Han Bila; its zone of responsibility was partly facing the army of the Bosnian Serbs, and it went, had a certain depth. The strength of this brigade was between 2.100 and 2.200 men. The 17th Krajina Brigade with its command post in the barracks in Travnik was created out of the 1st and 7th Krajina Brigades, and its strength was 3.300 men. In the territory of Travnik we also had the 27th Brigade, 27th Krajina Brigade, consisting mostly of Muslim refugees from Banja Luka and Prijedor. The strength was about 2.100 men. Its commander was Rasim Imamovic. In Travnik there was also the command of the third battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, Brigadier. What was the strength of the third battalion?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: About 900 men. And the command post was in Travnik, and the command of this brigade was in Zenica, which means that one battalion of that brigade was situated in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the El Mudzahid detachment; was it situated in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It's command post was in the village of Mecici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many men did it have?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: About 400 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, those are the foreign nationals that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I must also refer to the 7th Muslim Brigade which consisted of Muslim armed forces, those that I mentioned earlier on. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Also in Travnik there were the MUP units, the special police, the strength was about 800 men. Novi Travnik, in Novi Travnik the 308th Brigade was formed consisting of three detachments with a command post in Novi Travnik. It consisted of three battalions. The strength of this brigade was between 2.100 and 2.300 men. In addition to this brigade in Novi Travnik there was also a company of the 7th Muslim Brigade with about 100 men, and also, MUP units with about 200 men. In Novi Travnik we also had units of PPN, Sosna (Phoen).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They call themselves special purpose units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the function of those soldiers? What are they known for?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The function of this unit was actually, this was actually a private army financed by a man whose nickname was Sosa (Phoen). And its strength was about 100 men. In Vitez the 325th Brigade was formed consisting of former detachments with a command post in Vitez, and also belonging to it were three battalions, plus a manoeuvring or mobile battalion which continued to be an independent battalion within the composition of the brigade. And the strength of this brigade was 2.400 men, and the strength of the battalion was 3.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean 300?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, 300. Another company was formed in Vitez of the 7th Muslim Brigade consisting of about 100 men, and MUP units with about 60 men, 60 members. In Busovaca the 333rd Brigade was formed, its command post was in Busovaca. The strength of this brigade was about 2.100 men. In addition to this brigade there were also MUP units there numbering about 100 men. In Zenica there were four brigades. The 301st with a strength of about 2.100 men; the 303rd Mountain Brigade with about 1.800 men, and the command post was in Zenica; the 314th Mountain Brigade which will later become a motorised brigade numbering about 2.100 men; and the 330th Light Brigade numbering about 2.300 men, units of special purpose forces of the MUP had about 600 members. Typical of this period was the fact that the forces were reorganised, the forces of the Territorial Defence were reorganised to become the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the units came under the command of the 3rd Corps. They were linked to the command of the 3rd Corps, and that they were deployed mostly deep within this territory. But in Travnik I omitted to mention, too, special purpose units Mecici and Nanetovi; therefore, in addition to those mentioned, there were these units numbering 60 to 80 men each.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we describe these as more or less private units?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, they were more or less private units, and it was difficult to put them under the control of commands in the process of control and command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue. We're obviously now moving onto another period of time, perhaps we should go back to the previous map. Please let's go back to the previous period. Is it not functioning? Press it once again, please. There we are, that's it. So, we are now talking about the period from the 21st of January to the 30th of January, 1993. We have three indications as usual, the red for the Army of Republika Srpska, the green for the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the blue for the HVO. What does this map show?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, in this period from the 21st of January to the 30th of January 1993 the units of the 3rd Corps started regrouping of forces to form operative groups out of brigades, and then these operative groups were turned into tactical groups to facilitate the conduct of operations and the control in command when engaging in combat. So that in this period three operative groups were formed; the operative group of Bosanska-Krajina with its command post in Travnik, which included the following units: The 312th, the 506th, the 17th and the 27th Krajina Brigades and the 308th Mountain Brigade. The commander of this operative group was Mehmed Alagic. The operative group west which consisted of the units of the 307th, the 318th Brigade, its commander was Sermo Cikotic and the command post was in Bugojno. The operative group east, with its command post in Visoko. This operative group consisted of the units of the 302nd, the 323rd, the 303rd and parts of the 314th Brigades from Zenica. These operative groups were of a temporary nature, which means that their strength could vary; they could have more or less brigades under their command, depending on the assignments they were given. The operative groups had within their composition tactical groups which also carried out assignments along various axes. Those tactical groups could vary in composition ranging from one battalion to one or two brigades. The beginning of combat activities by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the area of the Lasva River valley started on the 20th to the 21st.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What month, you said between the 20th and the 21st; are you talking about January?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, January, 1993. These activities started with the setting up of a checkpoint in the Municipality of Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, this is the red dot that now appears towards the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. The forces of the operative group Bosanska-Krajina, together with the Lasva tactical group set up this checkpoint, and this marked the first open conflict. From the direction of the village of Kacuni where the communication was intercepted, interrupted between Busovaca and Kiseljak --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the main supply route going from Croatia through Herzegovina to this area, or was this of local significance?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This was the main road for providing supplies, both for the units and the population in the republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next in the next two or three days that followed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: On the 25th of January 1993 the forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina launched an attack from the direction of the village of Kacuni, and from the direction of the village of Merdani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What villages?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The villages of Lasva and the Ducine village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened there?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: On that occasion the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina took over these two villages of Lasva and Ducine, it took control of the villages and established a defence line, Lasva-Ducine-Kacuni, and thus completely cut off communication from Busovaca, the Kiseljak Busovaca line. At the same time the forces of the 333rd Brigade from Kacuni drew the line towards the communication, and therefore, cut off all communication. There was a complete cut off of communication from Kiseljak and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us that on the slide, please? You have gone onto the next slide. Can we take it back one? Let's go back a bit.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: So, communications were cut off at Kacuni and the villages of Ducine and Lasva were taken control of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we say that from that time on, actually, later on, were there no other conflicts in that sector around Bilaloci.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Let us now mention that within this context. At the same time, simultaneously, from 23rd of January, 1990 to up until the 24th of January, 1993, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina directed its forces from Kacuni in the direction of the Village of Bilalovac, where it expanded this communication road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: There is an error in transcript or translation. It was 23rd of January, 1993. So we're talking about January 1993 all the time. That is the date we're dealing with. So the communication was cut off, but does that mean that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in view of its operations towards Busovaca and Kacuni in depth established control of the territory, so horizontally and in depth, in width and in depth?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, the territory was extended from Kacuni, the whole of Kacuni, and the whole of Bilalovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina only control the road or the surrounding villages as well?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, all the surrounding villages, both on the left and right side of communication line in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since that time on, were you able to pass through that road without having an okay from the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No, we were not. We had to receive authorisation from the BiH army, or if we were accompanied by the UN forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In these operations that is here in this region the following units took part: The 301st, part of the unit from Zenica, that is the 301st and from the 303rd, 314th, 333rd Brigade because that was its zone of responsibility with its three battalions, part of the 310th Mountain Brigade from Fojnica, one battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade and units of the Manoeuvre or Mobile Detachment and one company of the military police from the 3rd Corps, the military police from the 3rd corps. From the operations that were conducted, we can conclude that the units of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army at this time in this period had taken over the villages of Busina-Lasva and cut through, cut away the enclave Kacuni-Bilalova. They cut the enclave into two parts, Kacuni-Bilalova at the Kacuni-Bilalova line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that time on, the operative zone for this region had an enclave at the Travnik, Novi Travnik, Vitez, Busovaca enclave and the second enclave, Kiseljak, Fojnica and the surrounding municipality?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: We now move on to this red area on the map. The red area represents the army of the Republic of Srpska. The green is the BH army and the blue is the HVO. In this period from the 15th of April to the 19th of April, 1993, the deployment and activities of the forces of the BH army, the forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as I say, took over combat activities in the following directions: Zenica, Cadaskuper and Zenica. In fact, Jezara, Podrica, Stranje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jezara is the great steel works in the Town of Zenica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these arrows now show the direction that the attacks of the BH army took and where the conflicts occurred with members of the Croatian Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: On this occasion, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina attacked from the two directions I mentioned and took over the control of the Croatian part of the Municipality of Zenica. On this occasion, an encirclement was formed and it took away the weapons of the two Croatian brigades there: The HVO. It disarmed them; took all the able-bodied men to Zenica, the KP centre there, detention centre there. A part of the units, which had succeeded in reaching Nova Bila via Nova Kar. Hand in hand with this operation, the forces of the 325th Mountain Brigade with its command in Vitez were reinforced with one battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade and one battalion of the 17th Krajina Brigade in the villages of Gacice, Donje Veceriska and Stari Vitez. They were holding preparations, making preparations for launching an attack on the main line, in the main direction. Kacuni-Babici. There are the arrows that are appearing on the screen now and continuing towards Gacice and Stari Vitez. The forces of the 325th Brigade, the second battalion, in the direction of Preocica, Krcevine, made preparations for launching an attack on Preocica, Stari Vitez and the attack in this direction with the aim of in these two directions of joining up with the forces in Stari Vitez and gaining control of the SPS locality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is SPS, when you say SPS?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It is the factory, explosives factory located there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By connecting these forces, would these enclaves, once again, be cut into smaller parts?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, joining these forces would mean cutting the enclave, Travnik-Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we have an onslaught on the cutting off of the road linking up Vitez and Busovaca, but we have an onslaught near to Bila?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, hand in hand with this operation and the main direction it took the forces of the 325th Brigade in the villages of Ahmici and Nadioci, and the forces of the 306th Brigade in the region of the Village of Grbavica were preparing to cut off communications between Vitez and Busovaca and Vitez-Nova Bila. In this way, they would ensure the free passage and it would be free for operations along the basic line of attack and would place under their control the factories of the military, the military factories, the SPS factory or the military factory for explosives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you have just said, do you consider that it was the main aim of the attack, the first aim to take over the explosives factory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a very exact piece of information that the special unit of the police from Sarajevo took part in the operation. What was its task?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The special position unit of MUP from Sarajevo had the task of -- that is to say, its members were professionals for explosives and it was their goal to safeguard the factory when the forces took control of the factory to see that no undesired incidents took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May we proceed now? If you have completed your picture of Vitez, can we look at the situation in Travnik, Novi Travnik, was there any fighting there or did relative peace reign there?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No, I was just going to say that the units of the 333rd Brigade were launching an attack from the direction of the Village of Loncari, Dusina and from the direction of the Village of Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the territory of the municipality of Busovaca and under the control of the HVO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's proceed. In the period between the 15th of 19th of April, were there any conflicts, any fighting there?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, there was, but they were, in fact, from a distance. They were attacks launched from a distance. There was no moving of forces towards the defence line and the HVO, so there was no combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next? Let us look at the situation in the municipalities of Vitez and Busovaca in the days to come. Once again, for the transcript, the yellow arrows are the direction of the attack of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the red points are the localities where they were confronted with the units of the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council? My mistake, green arrows, the green arrows denote the area of attack of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The distribution on this map, as on the previous maps, once again the red arrows denote the army of the Bosnian Serbs. The green arrows represent the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Not arrows, I am referring to the colour green. And the blue colour was the -- were the units of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we say that this map shows that some lines of the front have been established already because we see some contours of a future enclave, the shape that it was to take later on?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, we can. Some of the lines of the front have been established, such as the one towards Zenica and the front towards -- the front-line towards Novi Travnik. That is to say, in the zone of responsibility of the 325th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The distribution and activities of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the period ranging from the 25th of May to the 10th of June, 1993. After taking control of the Croatian areas around Zenica and cutting off communication between Busovaca and Kiseljak, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina moved its attack towards the area of the Lasva River Valley to Travnik, Novi Travnik, Vitez and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we say that this was a new offensive?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, we can. Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The beginning of the onslaught by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina started at the beginning of June with an attack on the command of the star headquarters of Travnik. And in this attack, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had managed make a complete surprise. They completely surprised their opponents and attacked the units holding the defence line towards the army of the Bosnian Serbs. First of all in Travnik and then in Novi Travnik --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to make it clear for the transcript, can you tell us exactly who attacked whom? Where were the HVO units located and at what time did the units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina attack and from what direction?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The units of the HVO held the line towards the Vlasic Plateau from Turbe up to the Lasva Gormila area, it is the area of the Municipality of Travnik. And it moved on towards this part, which was held by -- which was held towards Vocnjak. In the area of Novi Travnik, they held the line towards Palej and Komar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina launched an attack in Travnik with five brigades and reinforcements from Zenica, the 303rd, which launched an attack via Ovnak towards Guca. The 312th -- no, the 306th Brigade launched an attack on -- in the direction of Pokrajcici. The 312th, the 17th Krajina and the 27th Krajina and the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, launched attacks on units holding the defence line towards the army of the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The units of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, the units of HVO. The units of MUP, the Ministry of the Interior, encircled the star headquarters in Travnik and blocked them. At the same time, the 308th, working in cohorts with the 307th and 317th, launched an attack on the units holding the defence line towards the Bosnian Serbs in Kamenjas Mravinjak towards Goles and Komar. They were completely successful and took control of these positions. They captured the remaining part of the command in Travnik. The others retreated to the Vlasic Plateau where the Serbs took them prisoners and took them to the Manjaca Camp. And the same thing happened with the units of the HVO from Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You wished to say that in the Municipality of Travnik, the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina hit from the rear, the units of the HVO holding the front-line towards the Serbs and the HVO was not able to defend itself and then move to enemy territory where they were captured?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This is not what the witness said. If the witness intended to say that, I make an objection. And have the witness say that and not Mr. Nobilo say it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Brigadier, what is your answer to that? Forget what Mr. Nobilo said and give your own interpretation of the Bosnian army attack on Travnik in relation to the units which apparently were on this front. What is your answer?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I said that the units which withdrew across the territory, the defence line of the army of the Republic of Srpska were captured, were disarmed and taken to the Manjaca camp by the army of the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Have we completed this sequence? I think we need to take a break, but it might be best to finish with this series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one question. I just wanted to summarise. We do that very often here because he spoke of so many units that we laymen tend to get lost. So I wanted to make a summary and I think that is customary. But with what the witness has just said, I have just one question to ask to make it quite clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did the units of the HVO flee to the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Because they found themselves between two armies, positioned between two armies and they were attacked from the rear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: By the units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which can be seen from the maps that I presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, this would be a good time to break if you agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We'll take a 20 minute break and we'll start around 25 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We'll now resume the hearing, have the accused brought in, please. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, we're going to continue until 1.30, I think the witness will have to come back, because I'm sure that there is going to be a cross examination, so I suppose we come back on the 21st of September. You decide, let us continue now for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, after the break, let us continue. We ended with that unfortunate event in Travnik and the elimination of the HVO from the municipality of Travnik. So, please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, in the territory of the Municipality of Novi Travnik again a front line was established towards the Bosnian Serb army and they crossed over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me, sometimes there are, well, he said we would come back on the 21st of this month and it was transcribed as "settlement". It is 21st of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course, we agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I meant to say September and it came out as "settlement"; how can I make progress in English if that is going to happen? Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, let us be more precise, what do you mean capturing the lines. Where were the HVO troops and what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The HVO units were holding the defence lines at Kamenjas Mravinjaci towards the Bosnian Serb army. By carrying out an attack, the BH army attacked with three brigades, the 308th, the 307th, and the 317th, and parts of the El Mudzahid detachment, and a company of the 7th Muslim Brigade. They captured the existed, regulated lines facing the Bosnian Serbs, and as we will see later on, they gained control of the Croatian villages near Novi Travnik, Pecina, Rude, Jakovici, Kovacici Novkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, the Croatian population from Travnik and Novi Travnik; did they stay there or did they flee?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The inhabitants of these villages left, together with the army, crossing the territory of the Bosnian Serb army. In the territory of Vitez municipality the BH army carried out an attack with three brigades; the 325th Brigade, the 301st Brigade, from Zenica; and 330th Brigade from Zenica, with the second battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and with parts of the El Mudzahid detachment. The main objective was to link up with forces from Kruscica and from Poculice on the Poculice, Kacuni axis and the Bobasi axis, so as to capture the explosives factory in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that end? Did they capture the factory, or was the attack halted?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The attack was halted, or rather repulsed, and the lines did not change.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In the territory of Busovaca municipality at the same time the BH army attacked with three brigades; the 301st from Jajce, which was temporarily based in Zenica, that is where its command post was; the 333rd Brigade in Kacuni; and parts of the 314th Motorised Brigade from Zenica. In the region of the Lasva River special MUP units arrived from Sarajevo, and their task was, as we mentioned, to capture the explosives factory in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in the conflict in April, as well as the conflict in June, the main aim of the attack and of all combat activities was to gain control of the explosives factory in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In carrying out this attack one could call it an all-out attack against the Lasva River valley. The BH army had the support of a hundred mortars of 120 millimetres; ten Howitzers of 105, 155 and 122 millimetre calibre; eight to ten anti-air guns intended for targets in the air; 25 to 30 anti-air machine guns, also designed for action against targets in the air; two to three tanks; and two to three armoured weapons of 76 millimetre calibre known as Zis. With this strong military support they also used some of the artillery pieces directed towards the Bosnian Serb army. The basic goal of the army was to capture and place under its control the communication line going from Travnik through Vitez and Zenica, as well as the Zenica Visoko road, whereby it would gain control of the factory of military explosives in Vitez and also place under its control the entire Lasva River valley. One of the goals was actually achieved. The operative group of Bosanska-Krajina managed to link up with the operative group west, and the preconditions were established for capturing the factory. In this period the BH army did place under its control the factory, a special purpose factory called Bratsvo in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us what does that factory produce?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The factory produced artillery pieces from 60 to 122 millimetre calibre’s; that is, mortars of 60 and 120, and 122 millimetre Howitzers, as well as launchers of 128 millimetres. And they also assembled in that factory artillery pieces known as Oganj and Vatra (Phoen).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The deployment and activities shown on this map, the red stands for the front line towards the Bosnian Serb army; the green indicates the units of the BH army; and the blue are the HVO units. The deployment and activities of the BH army from the 5th of September 1993 until the 9th of January 1994, as the fundamental goals had not been achieved, the command of the BH army and of the 3rd Corps, making use of the advantages gained in its combat operations so far, carried out preparations for continuing combat operations so as to gain full control of the Lasva River valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, for the benefit of the transcript, we see on the map that the entire area of Travnik is fully in the hands of the BH army and that most of Novi Travnik, most of the actual town of Novi Travnik and the Municipality of Novi Travnik was also held by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Perhaps I should have pointed out that they gained full control the Novi Travnik and established a front line in the region of Nevic Polje and in Novi Travnik just below the Vilenica facility, across the village of Zubici and on to half the town. The front line in town was at the bus station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was the appearance of the enclave regarding the HVO in this period of time in the Lasva River valley. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The aim was to gain full control of the whole of the valley whereby they would have completed the process of military production.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say completed the process of production? Does that mean that in the whole structure of the military industry all that was lacking was an explosives factory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina lacked in the chain of production of military equipment, they lacked an explosives factory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said. Having captured the factory Novi Travnik all they needed to complete the chain of production was the explosives factory in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the BH army. I'm saying this for the benefit of the transcript, to make it clear.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. And they also needed to liberate territories to recircle the Muslims displaced from Bosanska-Krajina and other areas under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska, at the time the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said the main aim was the factory, you said they brought experts for explosives from Sarajevo, and now you said the second aim was to capture more territory to resettle Muslim refugees; how do you know this? How did you establish this fact?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
