utterances.text: With the arrival of the 1st and 7th, which later became the 17th Brigade, the Krajina Brigades from Bosanska Krajina, and also the refugees who were already there, when liberating the villages of Lasva and Dusina, refugees from Jajce were settled there immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean when the Croatian population moved out?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, when the Croats moved out refugees from Jajce were settled there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have information that certain military groupings already had designated how they would be settled?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I cannot confirm this data with any documents, but through talks we learned that the local people said, "Free some area for yourselves so that you can continue to live here in peace," and they advocated the policy of never returning to Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're talking about the Krajina brigades of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. The next task was to create the preconditions for further advancement in the Lasva River valley towards the south and the coast. The offensive of the BH army against the Lasva Valley can be said to have begun on the 5th of September 1993 with an attack on the village of Zabilje, from the position, from the feature Brdo. On this occasion units entered into the village to a certain extent. On the 18th of September 1993 the BH army carried out attack, an attack on the axis Kruscica-Preocica with the bulk of its forces, Kruscica, Bobasi, Kruscica, Gacice, SDS. And with additional forces in the area of Kruscica-Krcevine. Kruscica-Krcevine, and with this attack they wanted to interrupt communication between Nova Bila and Busovaca, and to create two more enclaves out of the existing enclave by a system of tightening of the encirclement, as it is known, until complete control of the territory was achieved. On the 5th of November, 1993, the BH army carried out an attack from Kruscica against the facility of Zabrige and the settlement of weekend houses. On the same occasion it gained control of the Zabrige feature and established a front line from the weekend homes to Bijelijna, which was just below the Zabrige feature. By capturing this feature the BH army actually had supervision over the SPS factory, that is the factory of military explosives called SBA, because it had it in its field of vision, and it also used infantry weapons in this operation. On the 12th of December 1993 the BH army carried out an attack from Preocica, Sivrino Selo and Pirici against Krizancevo Selo. At the command post of the second battalion of the 325th Brigade and the command of the 3rd Corps, heading these commands was army General Rasim Delic, who attended the execution of this operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the position of Rasim Delic at the time?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: At the time he was commander of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina managed to capture the village and to gain full control of this village, Krizancevo Selo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were killed; do you know?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: 74 people were killed in Krizancevo Selo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: On the 9th of January 1994 the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina continued its offensive from Krizancevo Selo. In the early hours of the morning it breaks through the front line and it manages to intercept the Nova Bila-Busovaca communication line and establishes the defence line next to the United Nations camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the casualties of this operation, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In Bukve Kuce there were 36 dead. That was the official report. And there are people from Krizancevo Selo on Bukve Kuce that are still listed as missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we talk about this front line and the casualties there, were these mostly civilians?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the command post of the second battalion of the 325th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In Poculice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In carrying out these operations the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina captured a strategic feature for us, that is the Zabrige feature, and it interrupted the line of communication between Nova Bila and Busovaca, the exit from Vitez to Busovaca, and it established the front line, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far the front was from the Vitez hotel, then?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The front line was 100 metres, about 100 metres as the crow flies from the Vitez hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You omitted to mention another position held by the BH army throughout this time in Stari Vitez; is it correct that the BH army was an enclave within an enclave in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, in Stari Vitez I may have omitted to say that there were forces the strength of a weak battalion of about 200 to 300 men, and throughout this period from the beginning of the war it existed there as a unit of the BH army. This slide would mark the end of my presentation as far as the Lasva River valley is concerned, the enclave of the Lasva River valley. On this slide you can see a map of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Once again, the mauve parts show the control of the territory under the army of the Republika Srpska. The green indicates control by the BH army, the yellow is the control exerted by the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which municipalities?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The Red Square shows the municipality for the Kiseljak, Fojica and Kresevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What date is that, please, on the map? What does the map refer to in terms of a date?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This introductory map represents the period of the Lasva agreement, the final appearance of the enclave at the end of the war -- the Washington agreement, I'm sorry, the Washington agreement. Yes, an error there in the transcript, the Washington agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Kiseljak, Fojnica and Kresevo, the deployment of the forces and activity of the BH army from May 1992 to April 1993. At end of 1992 the area of the Municipality of Kresevo, Kiseljak and Fojnica was under a complete encirclement by the BH army with the first operative group and operative group Istok, east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mention the operative groups, you have in mind the groups of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it is. My presentation refers to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The operative group Istok east with the command post in Visoko and the first operative group with the command post located on Igman. The composition of the operative groups was as follows: Operative group Istok east for this period of time had the following units; the 302nd from the Visoko Mountain Brigade; the 126th Brigade Ilijas; the 304th Brigade, Breza; the 309th Mountain Brigade of Kakanj; the units of MUP Visoko; and a detachment of the Abdul Atif with its command post in Visoko, let us recall, that was the unit which had Mujehadeen in its composition. The unit always had Mujehadeen, right up to the end of the war; so the El Mudzahid Unit and the Abdul Atif Unit had within its composition foreign citizens, and mostly they were commanders and soldiers of the unit as a whole. The first operative group within its composition had the following units: The 9th Mountain Brigade from Tarcin; the 145th Brigade; the 105th Mountain Brigade; and parts of the 4th Brigade, about one battalion strong. At the beginning of August the BH army, with its operative group east, Istok, launched an attack in the Municipality of Kiseljak and intercepted communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what point did this combat activity take place?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The village of Duhri, Han Ploca and Lepenica. And by doing this, they cut across the Lepenica valley from Kiseljak. At the same time they launched an attack along the Ostja Kokoska line with the objective of separating the HVO from the army of the Bosnian Serbs. Linking up the previous slide with this one and intercepting communication between Busovaca and Kiseljak on the 24th of January, 1993 the Istok operative group launched an attack from the direction of Kacuni in the direction of Bilalovac where it took control of the village of Bilalovac and extended its control in the territory. This links up the Istok, east operative group with the Zapad, west operative group. In the middle of March, the first operative group launched an attack along the valley of the River Neretvica towards Fojnica. The objective of this attack was to take control of the territory in the valley of the River Neretvica where there are over 20 Croatian villages and to link up with the forces of the second operative group -- no, with the Bosanska Krajina operative group, rather. And, with this, a connection would be made between the third and fourth corps via this first operative group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we not say that one of the strategic goals of the BH Army in Central Bosnia was precisely to link up their corps?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The operations were as follows and the civilian Croat population were taken out of the river upstream along the valley of the River Neretvica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, where did those inhabitants go to? Did they go to the under territory under HVO control in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, territory under the control of the HVO. One part was in Kiseljak and the other part towards Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue. These two pink arrows, what do they indicate?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The two pink arrows indicate that all communication had been completely cut off between Kiseljak and Busovaca. This brings us to the period from April 1993 to February 1994. The previous slide would have shown that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in its attacks launch had completely taken control of the valley of the River Neretvica and had linked up with the operative group Bosanska Krajina and the first operative group. In this period, after taking control of Bilalovac and cutting off the communication line between Kiseljak and Busovaca, by taking control of a substantial portion of the territory of the valley of the River Neretvica and linking up with the 4th corps, the army Chief of staff assessed that conditions were ripe. The army leadership decided that it was time to control the Lepenica and the Lasva Valley. I do not have a further precise detail because there was an interruption in communications between Busovaca, that is, and Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The positions that we can see now, the green denoting the BH Army, the blue colour for the Croatian Defence Council and the pink for the Army of the Republic of Srpska, those are the positions which you were able to monitor in detail up until the beginning of the war in April 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you place -- we have another date, February 1994, when the war ended and when peace ensued with the Washington agreement and where there was freedom of movement, what did you determine? Was the situation that you have on the map now, which you date in April, 1993, did the situation change? And if the some changes did take place, please explain them to us.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, there were changes, Mr. President and Your Honours. A change did occur after the signing of the Washington agreement because up until that time, the BH Army had taken control of Fojnica and the greater part of the Kresevo territory. And this line here was the official line after the Washington agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again an error in the transcript. My learned colleague, Mr. Hayman, has told me. The witness said that these changes occurred between April 1993 and the Washington agreement. After the Washington agreement, there was no fighting after February, 1994. And in the transcript it says that these changes took place after the Washington agreement. So the described changes occurred between April, that is the last moment when our witness could monitor the situation up until the Washington agreements; is that true? In the period between April and the Washington agreement?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the map we have double lines at the front for the Croatian Defence Council, the blue lines, what do these double lines show at Kresevo and in the direction of Fojnica between Fojnica and Kiseljak? What do these double lines mean?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They mean that the units of the HVO had returned, one, a part of the territory had regained control -- no, I apologise, the double lines, the Municipality of Fojnica in its entirety. And this double line, that is parts of the Municipality of Kiseljak and the Municipality of Kresevo. The area here was lost. The BH Army had gained it and reached those lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, the external circle, can we say that was the Front-line 1 and the internal circle, Front-line 2. And that is the last sustained, which you found after the Washington agreement when you returned to the territory of Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: On this map, you can see the zones of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The zones of responsibility, is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, the zones of responsibility of the BH army and of the army of the Republic of Srpska with the range of artillery, as well as the zones of responsibility of the operative groups of the 3rd corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, of BH Army. The red colour denotes part of the zone of responsibility of the Army of the Republic of Srpska of the 1st Krajina corps with its units, the 7th motorised unit, the 7th light brigade, mountain brigade, the 22nd light brigade and the 23rd light brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we're not interested in Serb units at this time. These are the positions of the army of the Republic of Srpska on this map.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: These are the positions of the artillery of the Republic of Srpska army and their range. I think we have another one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about these two positions? What do these symbols mean? Where is the gun and where is the range?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This is a Howitzer, a 122 millimetre Howitzer and the positions of the medium range weaponry and the mortars. The range of this artillery for the region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the shape, which is a little like a triangle and has a curved edge, within that area, guns from the positions of the Republic of Srpska army can reach any point within that area. If we look at the top left-hand corner, can you tell us what positions those are? What mountain is that on the map?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It is the plateau of Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we conclude that Zenica can be incorporated -- can be targeted from two points on the plateau, two positions on the plateau?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The transcript, once again it failed to include your answer. I asked whether this symbol of the triangle, which is curved along the edge means that from every point within that shape, that an artillery can reach any point. Artillery can reach to any point within that triangle. Can we conclude from this map that Zenica could have been hit without any difficulty from two artillery positions from the Republic of the Republic of Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The blue stands for the HVO units and their positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this yellow line?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This is the road, or rather, the communication that went from Prozor, Gornji Vakuf, Travnik, Vitez, Busovaca, Kiseljak, over which the war was being waged all this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is the main supply route?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, the main supply route for this area of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you tell me whether that typical of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as previous wars, the Second World War, due to the mountainous terrain of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that the war was mostly waged over communication lines because whoever has control over those lines controls the territory; is that conclusion correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. This applies in particular to Central Bosnia and this area where these operations were conducted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the main blood line or the line of life of this whole area was this communication line; wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. These blue dots mark the military industry facilities in Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was manufactured in Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Anti-tank mines in Bugojno and other mines in Novi Travnik. Artillery pieces in Travnik was a maintenance shop for communication means and also in the repair shops where the final assembly was done of vehicles for control and command at the level of the brigade and the marking was RS 30 E.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those are communication vehicles from which one can communicate?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is another blue dot in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In Zenica castings were manufactured for shells. And, in Konjic, in Konjic, ammunition from 7.62 to shells for guns of 20 and 40 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we say whether these were all factories established by the former JNA during the time of Yugoslavia that existed there from before?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at all those factories, is it correct to say that throughout the chain of production of military equipment and weapons, it was only Vitez, that is the explosives factory in Vitez that remained under the control of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it's time to break. The interpreters must be exhausted. So if you agree, maybe this would be a convenient time to break for lunch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I understand we're going to break for the rest of the afternoon at this point in time and not just for lunch. But my question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, as I remind you, we don't work on Friday afternoons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have a request. The testimony of Brigadier Zeko is extremely technical and complex. I would request, one, that the Defence provide to the Prosecutor's office a factual summary of the remainder of Brigadier Zeko's testimony. My second request is that the Defence provide to the Prosecutor's office copies of the various slides and variations of the slides. And thus far we've had twelve slides and subvariations of each of those. That they provide those to the Prosecutor's Office by Monday. Thirdly, that any additional slides and technical, illustrative aids be also provided to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Monday there is no hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President. But in order to properly prepare the cross-examination, the order of this Court is that the factual summaries be provided seven days in advance. These are more than just factual summaries, these are highly technical, highly complex illustrations. And, in order to properly analyse these illustrative aids and prepare for cross-examination, I would request that the Court order the Defence to provide those aids that have been used up to this point in time and will be used in the remainder of Brigadier Zeko's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would welcome the assistance of the technical booth in printing slides from the -- that is physical prints from the slides that we have depicted. We don't have them at this time and we have, in fact, spoken to the Court staff about the need to do that and it's simply a matter of getting it done. We're happy to provide that. I think there is only -- Mr. Nobilo can address what is left in the testimony there by way of these types of graphical and somewhat technical illustrations. We are near the end. Let me let him, perhaps, give Mr. Harmon some reassuring words in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: There are two requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we do not have a summary. We have the transcript and everything has been said in the transcript. It's in great detail and the Prosecution can use the transcript from these hearings. As my colleague has said, we would be glad to print these drawings and maps for the Prosecution, but we do not have any summary to give.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: There are two requests, if I have understood correctly. The Prosecutor is first of all asking that he be provided on paper with the slides, if that's what I have understood. There is no objection in principle on the part of the Defence, it's simply an assistance that's required from the technical services from the time that it would be needed to prepare them. I think that would be satisfactory to Mr. Harmon. Are we in agreement with that first point, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Prosecutor has also made a second request. You know that you must provide a summary to the Trial Chamber. I would like you to do it before the 21st of September for the other witnesses that you're going to call. That is for the rest of the witnesses that you call. It happens, let me remind you, that for this week we did not require that this be done. We asked for an oral summary, given the fact that the Trial Chamber's order had been issued on the 3rd of September. Further to your presentation, we would like you to make these summaries. Mr. Prosecutor, I think this does, in fact, cause somewhat of a problem. I would like to speak with my colleagues. In the middle of testimony, can we reverse an order that the Trial Chamber has already rendered? I would like to consult my colleagues on that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has taken a decision. We cannot go back on the decision of 3 September or on the decision taken the 1st day of this week when we made an exception to the written summary, which you must provide us with all the facts that you want to underscore. Furthermore, we cannot go back on that. The second comment is that if the Prosecutor is not ready to conduct his cross-examination, that is to do with effectively and appropriately from his point of view, he will always have the time to have the witness brought back. In the third place, if the Defence of its own will wishes to provide a summary of the facts about which it wishes to continue to question the witness, it can do so. That is with the Defence's discretion. If the Defence does not wish to at that time, the Prosecutor will be accorded the right to have the witness to come back for that part of the cross-examination that he needs him to come back for. If there are no other comments, I believe it is now time to adjourn this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 1.35 p.m., to be reconvened sine die.
